summary.headline: Coromandel Q4 FY26 revenue rose 19% to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA 16% to INR 494 crore, but reported PAT fell to INR 115 crore on last year's land-sale gain.
summary.overview: Q4 operations were strong: consolidated revenue grew 19% YoY to INR 6,068 crore and EBITDA rose 16% to INR 494 crore, with the fertilizer plants run full after the annual turnaround. Reported PAT of INR 115 crore compared with INR 578 crore last year, which included a INR 347 crore land-sale exceptional gain; this year carried a INR 71 crore impairment on drone-business investments and goodwill. Fertilizer margins compressed sharply as Middle East disruption spiked ammonia and sulphur prices, while crop protection, specialty nutrients, retail and NACL performed well. Management gave no quantitative guidance on fertilizer margins or subsidy outcomes, pending government support.

segments.name: Fertilizers (DAP/NPK/SSP/Nano)
segments.commentary: Record fertilizer production of 3.5 million tons and record DAP+NPK sales of 4.3 million tons (+7%), with 17.5% phosphatic market share; Q4 fertilizer manufacturing EBITDA was below INR 3,500 per ton versus over INR 5,000 per ton last year. SSP sales hit a record 8.4 lakh tons, and Nano DAP volumes grew 60% to about 42 lakh bottles.

segments.name: Crop protection (standalone)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose 15% to INR 3,054 crore and profit 55% to INR 569 crore for FY26; FY26 revenue mix was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore. Q4 standalone crop protection growth was about 2%, attributed to export sales being moved into Q1 and a bio export order shipped earlier.

segments.name: NACL (Nagarjuna Agrichem, 53% stake)
segments.commentary: Consolidated crop protection with NACL reached about INR 4,000 crore; NACL FY26 revenue INR 1,585 crore (+28%) and EBITDA INR 103 crore, with margin at 6-7% and guided to 9-10% next year.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail grew over 30% in FY26 with more than 300 new stores in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka, and entry into Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

segments.name: Dhaksha (drones, subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Impairment of INR 71 crore taken on investments and goodwill due to long lead times in order execution; management expects recovery after first large order executes this year.

guidance_outlook: Crop protection (standalone) revenue growth guided at 20-25% for the coming year, with domestic formulations growing 20-25% and six new product launches.
Sarigam active ingredient expansion of 20,000 tons is due around mid-2026 with payback under two years; Dahej Mancozeb debottlenecking of 10,000 tons has payback under one year.
Granulation capacity expansion expected to commission by December 2026.
Rock phosphate output in Senegal to rise 30-40% in FY27 from more than 3.5 lakh tons in FY26.
Trading margin of roughly 4-5% per ton; trading volumes may fall in Q1 FY27 on DAP availability, with second-half recovery expected.
Management declined to give fertilizer EBITDA per ton or margin guidance for FY27, citing fluid conditions and pending subsidy compensation.
Raw material cover secured for Q1 FY27; Q2 cover depends on Middle East resolution. Sulphur visibility is up to June.
capex_capacity: Kakinada: 2,000 tpd sulphuric acid and 650 tpd phosphoric acid plant commissioned in March 2026 (about 200,000 tons per year phosphoric acid); in trial runs, with stable operations expected from April-May 2026.
Dahej: technical plant commissioned in FY26 and Mancozeb capacity expanded by 10,000 tons; Sarigam expansion of 20,000 tons under way.
Technical MAP plant and seaweed granulation capacity under development.
Fluorination chemistry investment planned for CDMO opportunity; small-scale capacity to be created this year, production next year.
Coromandel has invested over INR 3,000 crore across segments in the last two years.
Coromandel's stake in the Senegal mining company increased to 71.5%.
demand_pricing: Industry: IMD forecasts below-normal monsoon for kharif 2026, though key southern markets are likely to see normal rainfall; updated IMD forecast due in late May.
NBS rates for kharif 2026 raised about 10% for N, P and S, which management said do not reflect the sharp rise in raw material prices and rupee depreciation.
Ammonia and sulphur are trading around USD 840-850 and USD 800 per ton respectively; phosphoric acid price for the quarter fixed at USD 1,360 versus USD 1,290 previously.
Q4 rupee range of 89.75-95.23 per USD; management said depreciation helps the crop protection export business.
Crop protection raw materials said to be covered, with input cost increases passed through; Mancozeb cost increases passed through to customers.
Rabi season demand was muted due to late monsoon withdrawal, with lower-than-expected liquidation.
Unique grades remained at about 35% of fertilizer sales on an annualized basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there a gap between consolidated and standalone P&L, and how will BMCC's depreciation and profitability evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said BMCC (mining) has turned profitable on better volumes and fixed-cost absorption, and the gap is mainly consolidation amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, not operating loss.

qa_highlights.question: How will fertilizer margins hold up given only about a 10% NBS increase against sharp raw material inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is seeking additional subsidy and cost-to-cost reimbursement for June-September, with discussions at an early stage; it declined to quantify the amount. Any remaining gap may be passed on through MRP corrections, and industry has already made some MRP corrections in the last one to two months.

qa_highlights.question: What are the crop protection growth, margin and NACL margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone crop protection targets 20-25% revenue growth with margins sustained near 19%; NACL margin improved to 6-7%, can reach 9-10% next year, and restoring 7-8% needs no major investment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year split of subsidy versus non-subsidy EBITDA and of crop protection revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Subsidy share of EBITDA was 57% in Q4 and 66% for FY26. Standalone FY26 crop protection revenue was exports INR 1,450 crore, domestic B2B INR 700 crore and formulations INR 900 crore; NACL FY26 revenue was INR 1,584 crore and Q4 INR 361 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the fertilizer finished goods inventory and trading exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished fertilizer inventory is about 5.5 lakh tons, of which trading is about 60,000-70,000 tons. Trading margin is roughly 4-5%, and FY27 trading volume may fall in Q1 because of DAP import shortages.

qa_highlights.question: Why was standalone crop protection growth only about 2% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 is off-season, export sales were deliberately moderated to shift into April-May, and a bio export order was executed earlier in December; full-year crop protection growth was 16%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sulphur and ammonia sourcing position, and is Q2 covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Sulphur has visibility up to June, with diversified spot sourcing from Canada, South Asia and Japan; ammonia and sulphur prices are about USD 800-850 per ton. Management said Q2 coverage depends on Strait of Hormuz shipping and a Middle East resolution.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for Dhaksha, the drone subsidiary?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said technical gaps are fixed and a large order is awaiting execution, with the first order this year expected to build confidence; a larger facility is due around May 2026.

risks_watch: Fertilizer margin squeeze: Q4 fertilizer manufacturing EBITDA fell below INR 3,500 per ton versus over INR 5,000 per ton last year; watch whether the June-September cost-to-cost subsidy reimbursement is granted and its size.
Raw material security: Q1 FY27 covered, Q2 depends on Strait of Hormuz shipping and a Middle East resolution; sulphur visibility only up to June; ammonia and sulphur around USD 800-850 per ton.
Subsidy receivables: outstanding INR 2,168 crore at end-March 2026 versus INR 1,654 crore a year earlier, though down from INR 3,785 crore at end-September.
Trading volumes may fall in Q1 FY27 on DAP import shortages, with trading margin of roughly 4-5% per ton; working-capital conservatism noted.
NACL margin recovery: 6-7% now, 9-10% guided next year, but management said restoring 7-8% is the limit without new active ingredients and formulations; 9(3) registrations take time.
Dhaksha drone subsidiary: INR 71 crore impairment; recovery depends on executing the large pending order this year.
Kharif demand: IMD below-normal monsoon forecast for kharif 2026 (updated forecast due late May); rabi demand was muted this year.

summary.management_tone: Confident on crop protection, retail, specialty nutrients and volume execution, but cautious and largely non-committal on fertilizer margins, subsidy quantum and timing, and FY27 EBITDA per ton, repeatedly saying the situation is fluid and declining to give numbers.
